article: The open toolbox for behavioral research
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A broad open behavioral-control toolbox with heterogeneous hardware and paradigms.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Frame PPS Toolkit as a continuing extensible research instrument with supported routes and example workflows, not as a finished theory test.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: Do not imply the same breadth of species, hardware, or maturity.

article: vexptoolbox: A software toolbox for human behavior studies using the Vizard virtual reality platform
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A domain-specific toolbox that fills missing trial-structure, randomization, recording, and standardized-output support around an existing presentation platform.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: State the domain barrier, then walk through how the toolkit turns PPS task structure into reusable files and runner outputs.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: Do not claim VR-style ecological validity; PPS Toolkit's domain is audio-tactile PPS acquisition and profile recreation.

article: Gorilla in our midst: An online behavioral experiment builder
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A graphical builder paper that connects usability, timing-sensitive tasks, deployment settings, and limitations.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Explain why GUI decisions matter scientifically and keep timing limitations visible.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: PPS Toolkit should not claim browser acquisition; hosted pages remain preview/orchestration surfaces.

article: PsychoPy2: Experiments in behavior made easy
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A mature experiment tool paper balancing graphical building, scripting flexibility, timing, hardware polling, and open-science reuse.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Use practical workflow language and describe what the builder records for reproducibility.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: PPS Toolkit is narrower and should avoid sounding like a general-purpose replacement for PsychoPy.

article: PsySuite: An android application designed to perform multimodal psychophysical testing
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A multimodal mobile psychophysics tool with stimulus accuracy, onset/offset, and cross-modal simultaneity validation.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: When describing audio-tactile routes, state what timing layer has been validated and on what device class.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: PPS Toolkit's Windows runner and phone/preview paths need route-specific validation; one route cannot stand in for all routes.

article: Delivering tactile stimuli via mobile browsers: A method for remote multisensory research
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A BRM tactile-delivery paper that separates behavioral replication from visual, auditory, and vibration timing characteristics.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Use it as a template for separating tactile software scheduling, actuator mechanics, and participant perception.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: Do not cite tactile scheduling as proof of Woojer mechanical onset or participant threshold stability.

article: Enhancing eye tracking for nonhuman primates and other subjects unable to follow instructions: Adaptive calibration and validation of Tobii eye trackers with the Titta toolbox
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A toolbox extension where calibration procedure, validation, and population-specific constraints are central methods contributions.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Model tactile-threshold calibration and adaptive safeguards as procedures with logs and validation boundaries.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: The two-miss tactile nudge is an operator safeguard until empirical bias/completeness evidence exists.

article: Evaluation of the Tobii EyeX Eye tracking controller and Matlab toolkit for research
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A low-cost device/toolkit paper that names accuracy, precision, latency, and unsuited use cases.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Use similarly explicit route suitability language for Komplete/Woojer/HRTF and profile-recreation claims.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: Do not let a working route become an unsupported universal hardware claim.

article: Mousetrap: An integrated, open-source mouse-tracking package
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A tool that integrates with a graphical experiment builder and carries data into analysis workflows.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Use it as a model for explaining the runner-to-analysis handoff while keeping analysis exploratory unless preregistered.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: Instant analysis should stay QC/exploratory, not a paper-level effect confirmation.

article: PyTrack: An end-to-end analysis toolkit for eye tracking
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: An open analysis toolkit paper covering raw-data extraction, visualization, and statistical comparison stages.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Make PPS Toolkit's analysis outputs legible as one layer in a larger analysis workflow.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: Do not imply automated model selection replaces preregistered confirmatory analysis.

article: Immersive VR for investigating threat avoidance: The VRthreat toolkit for Unity
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A domain toolkit for controlled but semi-naturalistic threat episodes with behavioral, movement, and eye-tracking outputs.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Useful style model for presenting PPS Toolkit as a suite of configured episodes/trials with output evidence.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: Do not blur immersive threat behavior with audio-tactile PPS unless the profile explicitly uses ecological/threat sounds.

article: Psynteract: A flexible, cross-platform, open framework for interactive experiments
why_similar_to_pps_toolkit: A framework paper that extends existing experiment builders rather than replacing stimulus presentation itself.
style_transfer_for_manuscript: Use it to clarify boundaries between dashboard orchestration, local companion/backend, native runner, and external LabRecorder/LSL tools.
caveat_for_pps_toolkit: Do not describe PPS Toolkit as a single monolith when evidence depends on route-specific components.
